analysis.investment_thesis: B.R.Goyal is a small-cap civil construction play trading at a P/E of 8.4 against 25.6% earnings CAGR — a PEG of ~0.33 that would normally excite me. But the 2025 revenue dip (589→510 Cr) and sharply negative operating cash flow (-36 Cr) muddy the growth story, making this a watch-list name rather than a table-pound buy.
key_strengths: Cheap on PEG — P/E 8.4 vs 25.6% PAT CAGR = ~0.33, classic Lynch territory
High promoter holding (73.6%) and solid returns — ROCE 17.9%, ROE 14.1%
Small cap (270 Cr) in India's infra tailwind — room to become a multi-bagger
key_risks: OCF collapsed to -36 Cr and FCF to -58 Cr in 2025 — working capital bloat typical of lumpy EPC contracts
Revenue fell 13% in 2025 (589→510 Cr) — growth story decelerating just as I'd want confirmation
Cyclical civil-construction sector with tiny FII interest (0.41%) and illiquid newly-listed stock (BSE 544335)
red_flags: Operating cash flow went sharply negative (-36 Cr) despite record PAT of 25 Cr — profits not converting to cash
Equity doubled (127→245 Cr) in 2025 suggesting recent IPO/dilution; borrowings also rose 49→77 Cr
analysis.detailed_analysis: What's the story? A Madhya Pradesh-based road/bridge builder riding India's infrastructure capex wave, doubled profits in two years (7→25 Cr), and trades at single-digit P/E. On paper the PEG of 0.33 is exactly the kind of mispricing I hunted at Magellan — a fast grower the market hasn't discovered yet, with promoters owning three-quarters of the company. ROCE of 17.9% is respectable for a contractor, and the balance sheet is reasonable (D/E ~0.31 post-IPO).
